topic.title: The Universe, gravity, eclipses and stellar life cycles
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: The Universe; TGS 2026-27: Earth and Space 2
topic.overview: Space is organised on enormous scales. Gravity shapes orbits and stellar mass determines how a star develops and ends.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: A planet orbits a star; a moon orbits a planet; a solar system lies within a galaxy; galaxies make up the Universe.
The Sun is one star in the Milky Way galaxy.
A light-year is a unit of distance: the distance light travels in one year.
Mass stays the same from planet to planet, but weight changes because gravitational field strength changes.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon is between Sun and Earth; a lunar eclipse occurs when Earth is between Sun and Moon.
Stars form from collapsing gas and dust in nebulae, become protostars and enter main sequence when fusion is stable.
Lower-mass stars end as white dwarfs; massive stars can undergo supernova and leave neutron stars or black holes.

practicals.title: Model eclipse alignment
practicals.aim: Use a lamp and spheres to model solar and lunar eclipses.
practicals.variables: IV: relative positions; DV: location of shadow; controls: sphere sizes/distances when comparing trials.
practicals.method: Use a lamp as Sun, larger sphere as Earth and smaller sphere as Moon; align and observe shadows for both arrangements.
practicals.expectedResult: Moon between Sun and Earth models solar eclipse; Earth between Sun and Moon models lunar eclipse.
practicals.safety: Do not stare into a bright lamp; keep cables secure.
practicals.evaluation: State that sizes and distances are not to scale and that the model simplifies three-dimensional orbital planes.

commonMistakes: Calling a light-year a unit of time.
Saying mass changes on another planet.
Using the same ending for every star regardless of mass.
examTips: For scales, build the nesting order.
For weight questions, use W = m x g and include N.
At every star-life branch, ask whether the star is lower mass or massive.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.title: Model eclipse alignment
practicals.aim: Use a lamp and spheres to model solar and lunar eclipses.
practicals.variables: IV: relative positions; DV: location of shadow; controls: sphere sizes/distances when comparing trials.
practicals.method: Use a lamp as Sun, larger sphere as Earth and smaller sphere as Moon; align and observe shadows for both arrangements.
practicals.expectedResult: Moon between Sun and Earth models solar eclipse; Earth between Sun and Moon models lunar eclipse.
practicals.safety: Do not stare into a bright lamp; keep cables secure.
practicals.evaluation: State that sizes and distances are not to scale and that the model simplifies three-dimensional orbital planes.
